Amazing game! I keep coming back to it. I loved Spelunky HD when it came out and remember playing it at work with couch multiplayer. When Spelunky 2’s development was announced, I was a bit worried they might ruin the greatness of HD. But when the trailer came out, I was so excited, especially about the liquid physics!

I played a bit on release, but it felt so much harder than HD that I took a break for a while. I ended up coming back about a year later and grinding out all the achievements with a coworker. I remember our first normal win and how satisfying that was! I also remember how thrilled I was to reach the Sunken City for the first time and actually beat the hard ending on that same attempt!

I then got into using mods and even started modding the game myself, which was a super fun way to get to know it better. After a little hiatus, I came back when I got my Steam Deck, for which this game is the PERFECT fit! I even wrote a small program to install Modlunky 2 on the Steam Deck with one click.

This is an amazing platformer that I just keep coming back to. The furthest I've gotten is 7-46, and I hope to reach 7-99 at some point!

Man, I LOVE this game. It teaches me that, karma really is out to get you.

I bomb a turkey, I die almost immediately after.
I let a magman blow up a shopkeep's items, I die almost immediately after.
I stomp on a leprechaun going after its gold in greed, I die almost immediately after.

It is the easily accessible game that teaches us all about karma. The no-nonsense, nonbiased way of introducing it. Once you get the hang of things, this 'karma' in this game, you'll get why you died in the game about exploring caves on the moon, in search of your long lost parents.

The original free gamemaker game is the original rogue-lite and everything about it has only gotten better in Spelunky HD and Spelunky 2.

One major feature is that you get everything up-front. There's no `unlocks` so all the progression involved is learning about the game and getting better. It makes for a bit steeper of learning curve to start, but feels much more satisfying over time and makes the game timeless.

The replay-ability is incredible. Plus all of the Easter eggs and side quests keep me coming back again and again. 10/10 recommend to anyone with time to kill because you'll find yourself playing this game over and over for hours on end. Good luck!

Spelunky 2's difficulty stems from the way all the individual mechanics interact. Mastering the game isn't necessary to have fun; Most people give up after a couple hours. There's nothing wrong with that, though it might help you to know that the game isn't made to be won. Rather, the building up of skill and the laughing at unexpected deaths is what brings out enjoyment for most people. I recommend this game if you enjoy playing games for the experience instead of the story or competition. Luckily, that's what I'm into.

While the game itself and it's mechanics are lovely, the game is too toxic.
The fact that you need to grind and grind mechanics and you can be killed at literally any step (or have debuffs that become critical sooner or later) makes it really frustrating. It gives you a high each time you do manage to pass checkpoints and that makes you try again and again and again. Abusing the inner mechanics of your head is a horrible practice in games today and I can't wait for it to become illegal (I hope it will, someday).
It would've been perfect if you could have an "easymode" for non-hardcore players. You need too big of a skillset to manage to finish it which can prove too frustrating for the common player, even skillful ones. As I said, you need to be hardcore to manage it. If you managed to finish the game then kudos to you, maybe I am just a bad player.

I love this game. The platforming, music, level design and procedural generation are all perfect. The attention to details about how different things interact with each other (even purely aesthetic interactions like how the horned lizards eat the bug critters and spew blood from their eyes on low health) is incredible and gives the game a lot of charm and really brings the world to life. It also makes the game very hard but rewarding, extremely re-playable and hilarious. I could play this game for 1000 more hours and still have so much fun and find new ways to die XD

The only thing missing is a shortcut to cosmic ocean, or an endless challenge. You can't lock away the best and hardest part of the game behind basically the entirety of the special ending route of the game like that and then expect the player to get through basically 100 more levels to win come on.

Spelunky 2 can be best described as addicting. Its controls are deceptively simple, and the game invites you with fun aesthetics and mechanics. You'll quickly hate every thing, from the bosses, to the first enemies to you encounter, to your very own whip. So why do I love it? Because every time you die it (extremely likely) it is your fault, and you feel like the next time you can do so much better. And when you are in the flow and grooving through the levels, nothing beats that feeling. Well, falling on spikes, getting frozen, anything in Neo-Babylon, and a lot more can beat the feeling, but hey, next time right? 9/10 game needs more moles

It's just not worth it. Go play Metroid.
